body:
Solution to the problem:
1. Use cmake 3.12.4 and above
2. Custom postgresql library path:
`cmake3 -DPOSTGRESQL_LIBPGPORT=/usr/pgsql-10/lib/libpgport.a -DPOSTGRESQL_LIBRARY=/usr/pgsql-10/lib/libpq.so -DPOSTGRESQL_INCLUDE_DIR=/usr/pgsql-10/include/server -DPQ_LIBRARY=/usr/pgsql-10/lib/libpq.a -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release ..`

Hi! Thanks for showing this.
Seems like a bug, client disconnected right after finishing transaction. And there is not proper code that will handle this situation. Beside noisy logging there is one more inportant downside: server connection will be expelled from pool, which is not good...
We will fix this, thanks!

> Hi! Thanks for showing this.
> Seems like a bug, client disconnected right after finishing transaction. And there is not proper code that will handle this situation. Beside noisy logging there is one more important downside: server connection will be expelled from pool, which is not good...
> We will fix this, thanks!

Thanks
I see some other errors if it helps:

This happens sometimes between  OD_DETACH errors:
```
(reset) not synchronized, closing
```

And sometimes these:

```
(main) ERROR 42501 permission denied for sequence session_sid_seq
(main) ERROR 42501 permission denied for sequence url_errors_id_seq
(main) server disconnected (read/write error): Connection timed out, status OD_ESERVER_WRITE
(main) server disconnected (read/write error): Connection timed out, status OD_ESERVER_READ
```

Thank you for your helping that i can build the odyssey in the CentOS 7 server within some warnings. 
I do not know it is successful setup of the installation the Odyssey. but now i can access through the odyssey port. 
In your thinking my installation config is right way to the installation step ?
If you have any opinion, please share to me. once again I really appreciate to your help.

Yes, but you can change order in different service backends. As discussed in the Slack channel. Probably, this is not very good solution. We want something to balance the stream of known-to-be-read-only queries between replicas. This totally makes sense.

Just to recap, so far, there seem to be two ideas on how to approach this.

One approach, as @x4m indicated is to enable Odyssey to be able to leverage `target_session_attrs`.
This would require that applications connecting have the knowledge of which query is "read only" and to also potentially "rotate" read only replica hosts in connection strings to avoid 1st replica specified getting all the queries (see prev comment about what docs specify)
 
Another approach is to have Odyssey parse the query and determine if it is "read only" and send it to replicas.
And its not only query parsing - proxy would have to potentially query PG catalog to determine which functions (used in queries) are "read only" safe...This is more complicated, and would add overhead to proxy for sure, with advantage that any application connecting via Odyssey could leverage load balancing without code changes...

You can reuse Machinarium, it's a coroutine engine designed to ease state-machine implementation of the protocol.
Normally you have to implement the protocol in a state machine to have async network usage, but with Machinarium, you can describe interaction as consecutive function calls. Machinarium will take care to seamlessly pass execution context to other coroutines, when you wait for network IO. This will be done without syscalls.

@x4m in your example, it seems like you're saying that even if `server_max_routing = 3`, odyssey may still open 6 backend connections to the storage because that setting controls CPU parallelism only (i.e. `server_max_routing` defaults to number of workers).

I get that, but ultimately what you're suggesting is that the maximum number of connections to the backend is really the sum of all `pool_size` connections being used (or rather all connections in use by each pool, but let's assume 100% usage). 

If I understood this correctly, then it becomes quite difficult to ensure a global odyssey backend limit when using a large number of users all being routed via the `default_db.default_user` route, because each user may consume up to `pool_size` N times.

pgbouncer has a `max_db_connections` setting precisely for this:

> Do not allow more than this many server connections per database (regardless of user). This considers the PgBouncer database that the client has connected to, not the PostgreSQL database of the outgoing connection.

Without this, dynamically scaling odyssey to N machines requires re-calculating all `pool_size` values across different machines and even that isn't trivial when using a default rule.

What do you recommend in this scenario?
